Send the application form, a recent transcript, proof of acceptance, two to four reference letters and either a one-page letter or a video of up to four minutes to the club by email.

title: Edmonton Chinese Bilingual Education Association Awards
audience: Students in Edmonton's Chinese Bilingual Program continuously since Grade 4
notes: The association does not publish the individual amounts or a closing date, only that applications open July 1. It has given 3,195 awards worth $400,450 since 1990, so the typical award is a few hundred dollars rather than a tuition cheque.
description: The Edmonton Chinese Bilingual Education Association gives awards to students in grades 6 through 12 who have been in Edmonton Chinese Bilingual Program continuously since Grade 4. Achievement is recognised across academics, leadership, community service, sports, culture, writing, dance and music, and applications are taken online from July 1.
metaDetail: Grades 6 to 12, with applications open from July 1.

title: Central Alberta Co-op Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 students in Central Alberta Co-op's trading area whose household has held a membership for at least a year
notes: The co-op states a fixed April 1 to April 30 window every year, so the dates here are that window rather than a guess. The membership test is on the household, not on you: a parent counts. Applications run through the Do Some Good platform, which needs its own account.
description: Central Alberta Co-op awards ten $1,000 scholarships each year to Grade 12 and mature students heading to post-secondary. There is no restriction on your field of study or which institution you attend. The applicant or an immediate family member must have been a Central Alberta Co-op member for at least one year with more than $2,500 in purchases over the past year, and must live in the co-op's trading area. The application asks for transcripts, two community reference letters, one education reference letter, proof of acceptance, and a 200 to 500 word essay on what the co-op means to you.

title: Rising Futures Scholarship
audience: Central Alberta students aged 25 or under who have received services from the Sheldon Kennedy Centre of Excellence or the Central Alberta Child Advocacy Centre
notes: The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it.
description: The Rising Futures Scholarship gives at least two students $10,000 each toward post-secondary, technical, or trade school. It is open to applicants who are planning to enrol as well as those already enrolled, so you can apply in your graduating year. Applicants must be 25 or younger and must have received services from the Sheldon Kennedy Centre of Excellence or the Central Alberta Child Advocacy Centre. The Community Foundation of Central Alberta pays the money to your institution, which credits it to your tuition account.

title: Shea Family Education Award
audience: Graduating students at H.J. Cody High School in Sylvan Lake
notes: The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it. Applications close at 4:30pm on the day of the deadline.
description: The Shea Family Education Award is $3,000 granted annually to one student graduating from H.J. Cody High School in Sylvan Lake. You apply through the Community Foundation of Central Alberta portal with a transcript or outline of your high school results, and proof that you have enrolled at a post-secondary institution. The application also asks for a parent or guardian Notice of Assessment, but you can still apply without one if you explain why.

title: Red Deer Golf and Country Club Centennial Scholarship
audience: Students graduating from a high school in Red Deer or Red Deer County who are involved in golf
notes: The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it. The reference letters are the part to start early on: you need two, each from a member of a golf club in the eligible area.
description: The Red Deer Golf and Country Club created this endowed fund for its centenary. Awards are made annually at no less than $1,000 to students who graduated from a high school in Red Deer or Red Deer County and are entering full-time study in a certificate, diploma, or degree program of at least two years at a recognized Canadian post-secondary institution. Applications need support letters from at least two members of a golf club within the eligible area. Selection is on merit, with preference possible for applicants who show financial need.

title: Smiles Thru Lindsey Women in Aviation Award
audience: Young women in Central Alberta pursuing a career in aviation
notes: The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it. The award page describes who it is for but does not spell out a grade requirement, so ask the foundation whether your year qualifies before you build a plan around it.
description: A $5,000 bursary for girls pursuing a career in aviation, created in memory of Lindsey More, who was training for her private pilot licence at Sky Wings Aviation Academy. Her family founded Smiles Thru Lindsey after her death in 2015 to raise suicide awareness and fund mental health education for youth in Central Alberta. The Community Foundation of Central Alberta releases the money to your post-secondary institution, which credits your tuition account.

title: Lorilei and Arthur Jenkins Collaborative Member Scholarship
audience: Current members of the Red Deer Royals heading to post-secondary
notes: The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it. Applications close at 4:30pm, and the portal needs its own account, so leave time for the two reference letters.
description: A $500 scholarship for current members of the Red Deer Royals, the city marching show band. You must be enrolling in or already attending a post-secondary program at an institution in Canada, so graduating members can apply. The application asks for a completed form and two reference letters, submitted through the Community Foundation of Central Alberta portal.

title: Red Deer Catholic Grade 12 Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 students in Red Deer Catholic Regional Schools
notes: The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it.
description: The Red Deer Regional Catholic Education Foundation awards $1,000 to Grade 12 students in Red Deer Catholic Schools taking the next step after high school. It is deliberately wide: a degree or certificate from an institution that grants formal accreditation counts, and so does educational training or certification aimed at the workplace, so trades and workplace training routes are eligible alongside university. Applications are submitted online.

title: Daughters of Wisdom Social Justice Award
audience: Students in Red Deer Catholic Regional Schools who demonstrate their faith through social justice action
notes: The foundation had not announced a date or an amount for this award when it was checked in August 2026; the page says only that applications are submitted online and the date is to be announced. Watch the foundation page, or ask the Superintendent office at 403-343-1055.
description: Established in 2012 by the Moore family to honour the Daughters of Wisdom, the religious order that founded Catholic education in Central Alberta. It goes annually to a student in Red Deer Catholic Regional Schools who demonstrates their faith through social justice action.

title: Ford Family Scholarship
audience: Graduating students at Penhold Crossing Secondary School
notes: The award page does not publish a deadline; it says each award has its own and directs applicants to the school. Ask the Penhold Crossing Secondary School office for the date and the application.
description: Three $10,000 scholarships are awarded annually at Penhold Crossing Secondary School, one each for Academic, Citizenship, and Applied or Practical Arts. You must have attended and taken the majority of your high school courses at the school, and be registered at a recognized Canadian post-secondary institution in a program of at least two years. Applications go through the school rather than the foundation, and the money is paid to your institution to defer registration costs.

title: Brady van der Heide Citizenship Award
audience: Students at Ecole Secondaire Lacombe Composite High School
notes: The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it. The award page does not state the amount.
description: A citizenship award for students at Ecole Secondaire Lacombe Composite High School. It looks for leadership, positive relationships with others, consideration for people around you, contribution to the community through volunteering or fundraising, reliability, and responsibility, rather than for marks. The Community Foundation of Central Alberta releases the funds to a post-secondary institution on the recipient behalf.

specificSchools: Ecole Secondaire Lacombe Composite High School

title: Health Care Professionals of Tomorrow Scholarship
audience: Graduating students who volunteer at Chinook Regional Hospital and are heading into a health care program
notes: The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it. Applications are due at noon, not end of day. The 40 volunteer hours are the gate to watch: they are lifetime hours at Chinook Regional Hospital specifically, so this is one to start in Grade 10 or 11 rather than in your graduating year.
description: Friends of Chinook Regional Hospital, the hospital foundation, and Alberta Health Services Volunteer Resources fund four scholarships a year. Two are set aside for graduating Grade 12 students, at $4,000 for first place and $3,000 for second. You must be an active, registered AHS volunteer at Chinook Regional Hospital with at least 40 lifetime hours, live in the hospital's service area, and be starting full-time post-secondary study in a health care field in the fall. Health care is defined broadly here and is not limited to careers giving direct patient care. Selection weighs your commitment to volunteering, why you volunteer, what your work contributed, your plans for a health care career, and your letters of support. Past recipients cannot apply again.

title: Ray Jolliffe Memorial Scholarship
audience: Canadian students entering theatre production design and management or media production and design
notes: The Allied Arts Council lists March 31 as the deadline without tying it to a year, so this looks like a fixed annual date rather than one cycle. It is a behind-the-scenes theatre award rather than a performance one, so the eligible programs are narrower than they first sound: production design and management, or media production and design.
description: Established by the Jolliffe family in 2008 to recognize Ray Jolliffe and his contribution to theatre production in Lethbridge. The scholarship is worth $3,000 and goes annually to a Canadian student studying theatre production design and management, or media production and design, at a recognized Canadian post-secondary institution. The Allied Arts Council of Lethbridge manages it on behalf of the family, with the funding held by the Community Foundation of Lethbridge and Southwestern Alberta.

title: Aspiring Artist Award
audience: Students in grades 9 through 12 in the Lethbridge area who are working artists
notes: The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. This one runs on nominations rather than applications, so you cannot simply put yourself forward: ask an art teacher, an instructor, or someone in the local arts community to nominate you. It is also open from Grade 9, which is earlier than almost anything else here.
description: Established by the Allied Arts Council of Lethbridge in 2019, the Aspiring Artist Award recognises a student in grades 9 through 12 whose level of achievement stands out against peers at a similar stage of development. The award is worth $1,000 and is meant to support both artistic work and further educational opportunities. Recipients are chosen from nominations made by the community.

title: Elsie Alexander Essay Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 students in the Lethbridge and district area who have shown leadership in encouraging respect for human life
notes: The 2026 cycle has closed and the association had not posted a 2027 date when this was checked in August 2026, so there is no deadline here to plan against. They run a newsletter that announces when applications reopen. The association draws its area wide: north to Nanton and Vulcan, east to the Saskatchewan border, south to the United States border, and west to the British Columbia border. You can apply for both of the Grade 12 awards, this one and the Elsie Alexander work and volunteer scholarship, in the same year.
description: An essay scholarship of $1,000 offered by the Lethbridge and District Pro-Life Association to a Grade 12 student. It is one of four awards the association gives each year, two for high school students and two for post-secondary students. Applicants are judged on having shown leadership in encouraging respect for all human life, and this is the award decided on a written submission rather than on service.

title: Elsie Alexander Work and Volunteer Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 students in the Lethbridge and district area with a record of pro-life work or volunteering
notes: The 2026 cycle has closed and the association had not posted a 2027 date when this was checked in August 2026, so there is no deadline here to plan against. They run a newsletter that announces when applications reopen. The association draws its area wide: north to Nanton and Vulcan, east to the Saskatchewan border, south to the United States border, and west to the British Columbia border. You can apply for both of the Grade 12 awards, this one and the Elsie Alexander essay scholarship, in the same year.
description: A $500 scholarship from the Lethbridge and District Pro-Life Association recognising work or volunteer service rather than a written submission. It is open to Grade 12 students who have shown leadership in encouraging respect for all human life. The association gives four awards a year, and this is the service half of the pair set aside for high school students.

title: Mac Nishiyama Memorial Scholarship
audience: Students graduating from a high school in southern Alberta and continuing to college or university
notes: The society does not publish a deadline or an application form on its site, so contact info@nikkeiculturalsociety.com for the date and the form. Its two pages also disagree on who can apply: the awards page says any southern Alberta high school graduate, while the society's about page describes it as being for students interested in Japanese language or culture. Ask which applies before you spend time on it.
description: A $500 scholarship awarded annually by the Nikkei Cultural Society, which is based in Lethbridge and supports Japanese Canadian culture in southern Alberta. The awards page states it is open to any student graduating from a high school in southern Alberta who will be continuing their studies at a college or university in the fall. The society also runs awards for University of Lethbridge Japanese language students and a professional development award, neither of which is open to high school students.

title: Cypress County Scholarship
audience: Cypress County residents in high school who are starting post-secondary
notes: This is the County Council award, which is separate from the Agricultural Service Board bursary that closes on the same date. You can be a candidate for both. What decides it is residency, not which school you attend: the terms of reference say applicants living in the County but attending high school in Medicine Hat, Brooks, Foremost or Bow Island are eligible, and so are students in the Crown Village of Ralston and the Townsite of Elkwater. You can only win it once. The application form is on the County's online registrations page, under Scholarship Application.
description: Cypress County Council awards two $1,000 scholarships a year to high school students from the County who are heading to post-secondary, with preference given to those entering a technical program. You need to be registered to start your first year, and the application wants a letter setting out your goals, your transcripts, and your letter of acceptance. A council committee picks the winners on citizenship and community involvement as well as marks.
metaDetail: Two are awarded a year; residency in the County is what counts.

title: Calgary Catholic School District Kerry Dyte Educational Scholarship
audience: Graduating Calgary Catholic students entering their first year with financial need
notes: This is the closest thing to a Calgary Catholic specific award on the Calgary Foundation list, which otherwise leans heavily toward the public board. The application asks you to show long-term volunteering rather than a one-off, and unusually it also asks you to show current part-time employment. The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it.
description: One scholarship of at least $4,000, paid straight to tuition, for a student graduating from a Calgary Catholic high school and heading into first year at a Canadian post-secondary. It was set up in 2005 so that money would not be the reason someone had to stop at Grade 12.

title: Fraser W. Lockwood Memorial Scholarship
audience: Graduating Calgary CBE or CCSD students entering first year, with a Filipino community connection preferred
notes: The scholarship honours the ties Fraser Lockwood and his family built with the Filipino community, and preference goes to students whose families have that connection. It is a preference and not a bar, so do not rule yourself out if you do not have it. The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it.
description: At least $2,500, renewable for three consecutive years if you stay full time. It goes to a student entering first year of undergraduate study immediately after graduating Grade 12 from a Calgary public or Catholic school, who has volunteered through a church, community organization, athletics, or cultural or political activity.

title: Julia Turnbull Leadership Award
audience: Graduating CBE, Calgary Catholic or Calgary charter school students active in student leadership
notes: Preference goes to students already engaged in student politics such as student council, a student union or Model UN, in youth councils or committees, or in debate and speech clubs. Charter school students are eligible here, which is rarer than it should be on this list. The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it.
description: Four or more awards of $1,500 each for graduating Grade 12 students going directly into first year of full-time undergraduate study. It looks for sustained school and community leadership shown through initiative and volunteering.

title: Michael Gee Scholarship Fund Award
audience: Graduating Calgary students playing U18 AA or U18 AAA hockey through Hockey Calgary
notes: You cannot apply for this one on your own strength alone: it needs a nomination letter from your coach setting out why you are a deserving player on the team. Open to male and female players at U18 AA or U18 AAA. The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it.
description: One award of $5,000, claimable when you start first year of undergraduate study. It is decided on character, hockey and marks together, and you need a cumulative Grade 12 average of at least 85%.

title: Owen Hart Foundation Awards
audience: Graduating students at six named Calgary high schools
notes: Eligibility is by school, not by board: Forest Lawn, Western Canada, Ernest Manning, Crescent Heights, Sir Winston Churchill and Lord Beaverbrook. You need a 70% average or acceptance to post-secondary on entry requirements, and preference goes to students holding part-time work. The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it.
description: Twelve or more awards of $4,000, two at each eligible school. One application is considered for both the Owen Hart Foundation Awards and, for Lord Beaverbrook students, the Jonathan Victor Trueman Memorial Awards, which recognise athletic achievement and artistic achievement in creative writing.

title: Bradley Hillmo Anderson Memorial Award
audience: Students in any year of a first undergraduate degree or diploma at a Calgary post-secondary
notes: Preference goes to applicants with sailing experience: Brad Anderson crewed on the Glenmore Reservoir and raced with the Glenmore Sailing Club. It is a preference rather than a requirement. The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it.
description: One or more awards of about $500 toward tuition, for students registered full time in their first undergraduate degree or diploma at a Calgary post-secondary institution with a GPA of at least 2.75. Entering first year counts, so you can apply in your graduating year.

title: Grace & Good Fortune Bursary for Single Mothers
audience: Single mothers in Calgary starting or continuing undergraduate study
notes: The listing does not restrict this to any particular year of study, so a student entering first year straight out of Grade 12 can apply. The application is built around an essay on your education and career plans and your experience as a single mother. The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it.
description: One or more bursaries of at least $2,000 for a single mother with one or more dependent children who lives in Calgary or the surrounding area and is attending undergraduate study at a Calgary post-secondary institution, full time or part time.

title: CEEA Indigenous Award
audience: First Nations, Metis and Inuit students entering first year of a petroleum-focused program
notes: The Canadian Energy Executive Association runs several awards through the Calgary Foundation, and this is the only one of them open to a student coming straight out of high school. The others all start at second year or later. You need a GPA of at least 2.7 or 70%. The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it.
description: One or more awards of $8,500 for diploma programs and $10,000 for degree programs, renewable for up to three consecutive years. It is for a First Nations, Metis or Inuit student going directly into first year of a full-time petroleum-focused program such as petroleum, mechanical or chemical engineering, geology, geophysics, or the matching engineering technology diplomas.

title: Bates Wardle Award for Lifeguards
audience: Students up to Grade 12 at named Cochrane and Innisfail schools training as lifeguards
notes: Eligibility runs by school: Bow Valley, Cochrane, St. Timothy Jr./Sr. High, Innisfail Middle, Innisfail High, St. Marguerite Bourgeoys, or Ecole Secondaire Notre Dame, with Innisfail catchment residency. Because it spans two towns with no facet of their own it sits under Alberta here. The reference letter is optional, which is unusual. The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it.
description: Two awards of $1,000, ideally one for an Innisfail student and one for a Cochrane student, paid through the school or post-secondary institution. It is for a student aged 12 through Grade 12 who is working toward lifeguard certification or advancing their training.

specificSchools: Ecole Secondaire Notre Dame High School

description: One award of $1,000 for a student graduating Grade 12 from a Wheatland County high school and enrolling in first year of a certificate, diploma or degree in any field at a Canadian post-secondary institution.

notes: Eligible schools are Foothills Composite High School, Holy Trinity Academy, St. Luke's Outreach Okotoks, Cameron Crossing School, and The Centre for Learning@HOME. The Rotary Club of Okotoks has run this since 2018. Okotoks has no region of its own here, so it sits under Alberta. The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it.
description: Two awards of $1,500 each, ideally one for a Christ the Redeemer Catholic Schools student and one for a Foothills School Division student, for graduating Grade 12 students entering an accredited Canadian post-secondary institution.

title: Kirby Morrow Memorial Scholarship

That is a very different kind of work from the rest of this list. The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it.
description: Two awards of $1,000 for an Alberta or British Columbia resident entering first or second year of a full-time undergraduate degree or diploma at an Alberta or BC institution, in theatre, theatre arts, drama, film, radio, television, animation or script writing.

title: Kids Cancer Care Derek Wandzura Memorial Scholarship
audience: Southern Alberta childhood cancer patients and survivors entering post-secondary
notes: Because it covers any year of study, a student entering first year straight from Grade 12 can apply. Southern Alberta here means Red Deer and everything east, west and south of it. You cannot hold this and the Kids with Cancer Society Bursary, which is the northern Alberta equivalent. description: Awards vary each year but start at $2,500, with more available where cancer has caused extenuating circumstances. It is for a childhood cancer patient or survivor diagnosed at age 18 or younger who lives in southern Alberta and is enrolled in any year of an undergraduate degree, diploma or certificate.

title: Smillie Family Education Award
audience: Students from rural Canadian communities entering agriculture, education or health care
notes: It asks for a GPA of at least 2.7 or 70% together with financial need, and for leadership and volunteering in both school and community. The rural residency is the real filter here rather than any particular province. The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it.
description: Three awards of about $2,000 each for a Canadian citizen or permanent resident who has lived in a rural Canadian community and is entering first or second year of a full-time undergraduate degree or diploma leading to a career in agriculture, education or health care.

title: Shelagh Neary Mikulak Memorial Scholarship for Leadership and Innovation in Library Sciences
audience: Students in a library sciences or library technician program in any year of study
notes: It is open to any year of study, so a student starting a library technician diploma straight out of Grade 12 qualifies. It is a narrow field but a genuinely open door, and it needs a GPA of at least 2.7 or 70% plus demonstrated financial need. The provider had not posted a date for the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward. Confirm before you plan around it.
description: Two awards of about $2,500, preferably one to an undergraduate and one to a graduate student, for someone enrolled in a Library and Information Sciences or Library Technician certificate, diploma or graduate program at a Canadian post-secondary institution.

title: Royal Canadian Legion Branch 288 Scholarship
audience: Graduates of any Airdrie high school entering first year at the University of Calgary
notes: There is no separate form. You are considered through the High School Awards section of the My UCalgary portal once you have applied for admission, so the work is finishing that section rather than writing anything new. The award page publishes no closing date, which means the admission timeline is the one that matters.
description: Three awards of up to $1,300 each, funded by Airdrie's Royal Canadian Legion branch, for graduates of any Airdrie high school entering their first year at the University of Calgary in any faculty. Selection is on academic merit, and the award carries no citizenship or residency requirement beyond the Airdrie school.
metaDetail: Three awards for Airdrie graduates heading to UCalgary.

title: Airdrie and District Agricultural Society Scholarship
audience: Airdrie area students heading to post-secondary, one award for agricultural studies and one for anything else
notes: The society does not publish the award value. Applications go by email to airdrieagsocietysocial@gmail.com, and the essay topic has been the same one for years, so it can be drafted well before September. The non-agricultural award is the one students skip, which is exactly why it is worth an evening.
description: Two scholarships a year from the Airdrie and District Agricultural Society, one for a student entering agricultural studies and one for a student entering anything else. It asks for a 250 to 300 word essay on the value of volunteerism, three years of extracurricular and leadership activity, and a transcript that includes Grade 12 marks.
metaDetail: Two local awards, one of them open to any field.

title: Rocky View Teachers' Scholarship
audience: Rocky View Schools graduates, and children of ATA Local 35 members graduating anywhere in Alberta
notes: The teachers fund this themselves out of ATA Local 35, and in 2022-23 the pool was about $90,000. Proof of enrolment is the catch: a letter of acceptance does not count, so you apply after you have registered, not when you get in. The forms are Cognito forms and do not work properly on a phone.
description: Rocky View teachers fund a set of scholarships each year for students graduating from a Rocky View high school, which covers the Airdrie public schools, and for children of ATA Local 35 members graduating from any Alberta high school. A Certificate of Achievement qualifies as well as a diploma. Applications opened May 1 and close September 30, the fall after you graduate.
metaDetail: Applied the fall after you graduate, with proof of enrolment.

title: Rocky View County 4-H Scholarship
audience: 4-H members from a Rocky View District club entering or returning to post-secondary
notes: Three years in a Rocky View District club is the real filter, and it is one you cannot fix in your Grade 12 year. It is a one-time award, so it cannot be won twice. Applications run through the 4-H Alberta registration site rather than the county's own page. The May 15 date is this year's rolled forward, since the county had not posted the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026.
description: Rocky View County funds two $500 scholarships a year for 4-H members entering or returning to post-secondary study. You need at least three years of membership in a club in the Rocky View District, which takes in the country around Airdrie, and the award can only be held once.
metaDetail: Two awards, and three years in a Rocky View club.

title: Rocky View County Agricultural Scholarship at Olds College
audience: Rocky View County residents in Agricultural Production or Land and Water Resources at Olds College
notes: Two intakes rather than one: October 15 for the fall term and December 31 for winter. Residency is in the county itself, so a student inside Airdrie's city limits does not qualify for this one even though the rest of the page applies to them. The application is Olds College's own awards portal.
description: A $500 award for a Rocky View County resident in the first or second year of the Agricultural Production or the Land and Water Resources program at Olds College, with a GPA of at least 3.00. The county funds it and Olds College administers it through its awards portal.
metaDetail: County residents only, with a fall and a winter intake.

title: Sean Smith Memorial Scholarship
audience: Current or former Airdrie Minor Basketball players enrolled full time in post-secondary
notes: AMBA's page still advertises the 2023-24 window, January 8 to February 26, so this date is that cycle rolled forward and worth confirming in January. Essays are stripped of names before the committee reads them. A past AMBA scholarship winner cannot win again.
description: One $500 award from Airdrie Minor Basketball for a current or former AMBA player who is enrolled full time in a post-secondary program. It is named for Sean Smith and marks sportsmanship and team spirit rather than scoring. The application is a short essay, and proof of enrolment is required before the money is paid out.
metaDetail: A short essay, and a very small applicant pool.

title: Colin McKenna Memorial Scholarship
audience: Current or former Airdrie Minor Basketball coaches, referees, volunteers and board members in post-secondary
notes: This is the one to read twice: it is not for players. If you have refereed a season of mini ball or helped run a tournament, you are the intended applicant, and almost nobody applies. AMBA's page still shows the 2023-24 window of January 8 to February 26, so this date is that cycle rolled forward.
description: One $500 award from Airdrie Minor Basketball for someone who gave time to the association off the court, as a coach, referee, volunteer or board member, and is now enrolled full time in post-secondary study. It honours Colin McKenna's work building basketball in Airdrie. The application is a short essay judged blind.
metaDetail: For the volunteers and referees, not the players.

title: Airdrie Rotary Festival of Performing Arts Scholarships
audience: Performers who live or study music in Airdrie and Rocky View County
notes: A recent festival handed out 62 scholarships worth just under $5,000 in total, so treat these as many small awards rather than one large one. Two rules decide most of it: the piece has to be memorized, and you need the top mark in your class or at least 85 per cent. The 2026 festival ran March 16 to 26; registration for the next one opens through MusicFestivalSuite and the site had not posted its dates when this was checked.
description: The Airdrie Rotary festival attaches scholarships to its music and speech classes, awarded to competitors who take the highest mark in their class or earn at least 85 per cent. You have to live or study music in Rocky View County to be eligible, and students away at post-secondary can still qualify through a parent living in the county.
metaDetail: Many small awards, decided by your festival mark.

title: Jack Paterson Memorial Scholarship
audience: Alberta students aged 17 to 25 who volunteer in the Bow Valley Credit Union service area
notes: The volunteering has to be in one of the credit union's own communities: Acheson, Airdrie, Banff, Calgary, Canmore or Cochrane, and within the last two years. You do not have to bank there. Applications run June 17 to August 31, results by September 16 and money by September 30, which makes this one of the few awards that pays in time for the fall term.
description: A single $4,000 award from Bow Valley Credit Union for an Alberta student between 17 and 25 who is enrolled or accepted full time at a Canadian post-secondary institution and has volunteered in the credit union's service area in the past two years. You submit proof of enrolment, proof of Alberta residency, a resume, and a statement or video about your goals.
metaDetail: Volunteering in the credit union's own towns is the filter.

title: Bow Valley Credit Union Scholarship
audience: Alberta students aged 17 to 25 entering or continuing full-time post-secondary study
notes: Two awards, and no membership requirement: the credit union asks for Alberta residency, not an account. The same June 17 to August 31 window as the Jack Paterson award, and one application covers what you qualify for. Trades and technical programs count.
description: Two $2,000 scholarships from Bow Valley Credit Union for Alberta residents between 17 and 25 who are enrolled or accepted at an accredited Canadian post-secondary institution in a full-time undergraduate or technical program. The application asks for proof of enrolment, proof of Alberta residency, a resume, and a short statement or video about your educational goals.
metaDetail: No membership needed, and trades programs count.

title: Anne Beaty Memorial Scholarship
audience: Alberta high school students and graduates headed into writing, journalism or communications
notes: Run by the Airdrie magazine airdrielife, in memory of a writer who worked there and at the Airdrie Public Library. The selection committee includes her two daughters and the magazine's publisher, which tells you the application is read by people looking for a voice rather than a transcript. The magazine does not publish an amount or a fixed closing date, so watch its site in the spring.
description: An annual award from airdrielife magazine for an Alberta high school student or graduate who is serious about the written word, going to one applicant a year on academic record, community involvement and leadership. It was created in 2017 in memory of Anne Beaty, who wrote for the magazine from 2010 to 2016.
metaDetail: One recipient a year, chosen for the writing.

title: Calgary Black Chambers Business Scholarship
audience: Black students in a Commerce or Business Administration program, entering second year or beyond
notes: One application is considered for all four awards, so there is nothing to gain from picking one. The geography is wider than the name suggests: a graduate of an Airdrie, Chestermere, Cochrane, Diamond Valley, High River, Okotoks, Springbank or Strathmore high school qualifies at any Canadian institution, and everyone else has to be at a Calgary one. The provider had not posted the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward.
description: Four awards for Black Canadian citizens or permanent residents in a full-time Commerce or Business Administration degree or diploma, entering second year or beyond: the ATB Community Leadership Scholarship and the KPMG Academic Excellence Scholarship at $5,000, and the Academic Excellence at MRU and TD Business Leadership scholarships at $7,000. It needs a GPA of at least 2.7 or 70 per cent and one reference letter from a business or community leader.
metaDetail: One application, four awards, second year and beyond.

title: Calgary Black Chambers Legacy Scholarship
audience: Black students entering second year or beyond of a first undergraduate degree or diploma
notes: Eight awards makes this one of the better odds in the Calgary Foundation's list, and it is the continuing-student twin of the Legacy Entrance Scholarship rather than a competitor to it. Graduates of an Airdrie, Chestermere, Cochrane, Diamond Valley, High River, Okotoks, Springbank or Strathmore high school qualify wherever in Canada they are studying. The provider had not posted the new cycle when this was checked in August 2026, so this is last cycle's deadline rolled forward.
description: Eight awards of $2,500 each for Black Canadian citizens or permanent residents entering second year or beyond of a first undergraduate degree or diploma in full-time study. It asks for a GPA of at least 2.7 or 70 per cent, demonstrated financial need, school or community involvement, and one reference letter.
metaDetail: Eight awards, for students already at post-secondary.

title: Northwestern Alberta Foundation Student Awards
audience: Students from northwestern Alberta entering or continuing post-secondary study
notes: This is the single most useful application in the Peace Country and almost nobody outside Grande Prairie has heard of it. The foundation holds more than forty separate award funds, and one universal form puts you in front of every fund you qualify for, so the work of applying once is spread across dozens of chances. In 2025 it paid out over $60,000 across 100 awards. The window ran from April 16 to August 9 in 2026, so this is that deadline rolled forward a year and the foundation had not posted the new dates when this was checked.
description: One application to the Northwestern Alberta Foundation is considered for over forty student award funds covering sports, nursing, environmental studies, emergency services, trades, agriculture, fine arts, animal health, education, business, technology, music, tourism and hospitality. Recipients come from Grande Prairie, Peace River, High Level and other communities across the region, and awards follow students to institutions inside and outside Alberta. Decisions are sent in mid-September.
metaDetail: One form, over forty separate award funds.

title: Ron Pfau Memorial Scholarship
audience: County of Grande Prairie residents studying business, commerce or public office administration
notes: Named for a longtime County administrator, and the residency test is the County of Grande Prairie rather than the City, so a student inside city limits does not qualify on their own address. Your parents' County residence counts if you have moved away for school. County council handed administration to the Northwestern Alberta Foundation in 2024, so it now runs on the foundation's universal application and its August deadline, shown here rolled forward.
description: A $1,000 scholarship for current or former residents of the County of Grande Prairie who are Canadian citizens or landed immigrants and are entering or enrolled at an Alberta post-secondary institution in business, commerce or public office administration. Applications go through the Northwestern Alberta Foundation portal.
metaDetail: County address required, not a city one.

title: Grande Prairie Auto Group Student Award
audience: Grande Prairie city or county residents in an Automotive Service Technician program
notes: A single award, but the eligible pool is tiny: you have to live in the City or County of Grande Prairie and be registered specifically as an automotive service technician. If that is you, this is close to the best odds on the site. Five dealership general managers put it together in 2022. It is paid through the Northwestern Alberta Foundation universal application, so the deadline shown is the foundation's, rolled forward a year.
description: One award of $1,500 for a resident of the City of Grande Prairie or the County of Grande Prairie who is registered in an Automotive Service Technician program. Applications are made through the Northwestern Alberta Foundation.
metaDetail: One award, and a very small eligible pool.

title: Chief Ronald W. Clarke Fund Student Award
audience: County of Grande Prairie residents in an emergency services program
notes: The Wembley Fire Department started this in 2012 for a volunteer firefighter with 46 years of service, and the eligible programs are broader than the name suggests: nursing and physician studies count alongside firefighting and paramedicine. The fund is an endowment, so the amount depends on what it earned that year and the foundation does not publish a fixed figure. Applications run through the foundation's universal form and its August deadline, shown here rolled forward.
description: A student award for a resident of the County of Grande Prairie registered in an emergency services program, including firefighting, emergency medical services, paramedic training, nursing, physician services and enforcement services. Applicants are asked to show commitment or roots in the Peace Country. Applications are made through the Northwestern Alberta Foundation.
metaDetail: Nursing counts, not just firefighting.

title: Royal Canadian Legion Branch 54 Bursary
audience: Grande Prairie graduates with veteran ancestry
notes: Four bursaries, and the ancestry test is wider than most students assume: a grandparent or great-grandparent who served is usually enough, and the branch will tell you if you are unsure. Any program of study qualifies, which is rarer than it sounds among Legion awards. This is last cycle's August deadline rolled forward a year, since the branch had not posted the new one when this was checked.
description: Four bursaries of $750 for students who have completed Grade 12, are residents of the City or County of Grande Prairie graduating from a local high school, and are descended from a veteran. The award is open to any program of post-secondary study.
metaDetail: Four awards, and any program qualifies.

title: Grande Prairie and District Oldtimers' Association Scholarship
audience: Descendants of Grande Prairie district pioneers
notes: The eligibility line here is genuinely unusual and it is worth asking your family about before you rule yourself out: you have to be descended from a Grande Prairie district pioneer family. Many students in the Peace Country qualify and never check. The academic bar is a 70 per cent average, which is low by scholarship standards, and the association does not publish a fixed amount.
description: A scholarship for post-secondary students who are descendants of Grande Prairie district pioneers and who have maintained a minimum 70 per cent average. The value is set by the association each year.
metaDetail: For pioneer descendants, at a 70 per cent bar.

title: Perky McCullough International Excellence Scholarship
audience: Grande Prairie athletes competing at the international level
notes: The bar is real: this is for athletes with a credible path to international competition, and you need confirmation of membership in a national sport association to apply. Two awards a year. One catch that disqualifies people every cycle is that an application submitted after the event has already happened is not eligible, so apply ahead of the competition you are funding.
description: Two scholarships of $2,500 a year from the City of Grande Prairie for athletes who are or have been part of the Grande Prairie Sport Development System and show the best potential for international success. The application asks for letters of support from a coach or mentor, confirmation of national sport association membership, a goal statement covering short and long term objectives, and disclosure of other funding and sponsorships.
metaDetail: Two awards, and you must apply before the event.

title: Bob Neufeld Scholarship
audience: Grande Prairie athletes, volunteer coaches and sport officials
notes: Four awards, and this is one of the few sport scholarships anywhere that treats volunteer coaches and officials as equals with athletes, so a Grade 12 student who referees or coaches a younger division can apply on that alone. Clubs are limited to one applicant per deadline, so ask early rather than assuming your club has a spot. As with the other City award, you have to apply before the event happens.
description: Up to four scholarships of $1,200 a year from the City of Grande Prairie for individuals pursuing excellence in their sport. Individual athletes, volunteer coaches and sport officials may all apply, and the application asks for a goal statement with performance history, letters of support from a coach or mentor, and confirmation of national sport association membership.
metaDetail: Coaches and referees apply on equal footing.

title: Rotary Club of Grande Prairie Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 students at Grande Prairie high schools
notes: One of the awards is set aside for a student heading to trade school rather than university, which is worth knowing because trades applicants often skip Rotary awards assuming they are a poor fit. The application is built around a personal statement on Rotary's core values of service, integrity, leadership and diversity, so write to those four words directly. This is last cycle's May deadline rolled forward a year.
description: A $2,000 scholarship from the Rotary Club of Grande Prairie for Grade 12 students at local high schools who are completing diploma requirements and are registered for full-time post-secondary study starting the fall after graduation. One award is available for a student entering a trade school program of at least six months. The application requires a personal statement on Rotary's core values and two letters of reference.
metaDetail: One award is reserved for trade school.

title: Weyerhaeuser Grande Prairie Local Scholarship
audience: Grande Prairie Public School Division graduates
notes: Two awards, restricted to graduates of the public division, so Catholic and Peace Wapiti students are out. Certain programs get preference and the application form is where that list lives, so read it before you write anything. Awards are presented at the division's Striving for Excellence dinner in October, months after you graduate. This is last cycle's deadline rolled forward.
description: Two scholarships of $500 each from Weyerhaeuser for Grande Prairie Public School Division graduates. Preference is given to students entering specific programs identified on the application form.
metaDetail: Public division graduates only.

title: GPPSD Career and Technology Studies Scholarship
audience: Grande Prairie Public School Division students in CTS courses
notes: The Education Foundation funds two of these at each of the division's two high schools, so four are given out and the pool is only students taking CTS courses at those schools. That is unusually good odds for a $1,000 award. The division's page was still showing an old cycle's dates when this was checked, so confirm the current deadline with your counsellor rather than trusting the posted one.
description: Scholarships of $1,000 for Grande Prairie Public School Division students studying welding, construction, fashion design, automotive technology, design studies, cosmetology, foods, electronics, communications or business education. Awards are presented at the division's Striving for Excellence Awards Dinner.
metaDetail: Two per school, for CTS students.

title: Striving for Nursing Excellence Bursary
audience: Students in nursing programs in the Grande Prairie region
notes: The range is wide because the committee sizes the award to the applicant, so a strong file is worth applying with even if you only need part of it. Every nursing credential is eligible, from licensed practical nursing through to a doctorate, which makes this unusually open compared to most nursing awards. Applications go by email to the hospital foundation. This is last cycle's May deadline rolled forward a year.
description: A bursary of between $500 and $5,000 from the Grande Prairie Regional Hospital Foundation for students in licensed practical nursing, nursing, psychiatric nursing, nurse practitioner, master of nursing or nursing doctorate programs. The committee looks for commitment, dedication and growth potential. The application asks for a cover letter, resume, two letters of reference, a course outline and transcripts.
metaDetail: Every nursing credential qualifies, LPN through doctorate.

title: Sarah Joan Alward Bursary
audience: Health care students who will work in northwestern Alberta
notes: The catch is the return of service agreement: taking this money commits you to a year of work in northwestern Alberta after you finish. If you were planning to come home anyway that is free money, and if you were not, read the agreement before you sign. You also need at least one year of study already completed, so this is not an award to apply for in Grade 12.
description: A bursary of between $1,000 and $2,500 from the Grande Prairie Regional Hospital Foundation for students in a health care field who have completed at least one year at an accredited institution, are filling an identified occupational need in northwestern Alberta, and will sign a one year return of service agreement.
metaDetail: Comes with a one year return of service.

title: Northern Alberta Rural Physicians Fund
audience: Medical students who attended high school in northern Alberta
notes: The eligibility line is drawn on a map: you had to attend high school in an Alberta community at or north of the 54th parallel, which takes in Grande Prairie, Peace River, High Level, Fort McMurray and Grande Cache. Worth flagging in Grade 12 even though you cannot apply yet, because it is a reason to keep your northern high school records handy years later.
description: One or more awards totalling up to $10,000 a year from the Grande Prairie Regional Hospital Foundation for medical students accepted at or enrolled in a Canadian medical school who intend to practise in rural northern Alberta at or north of the 54th parallel. Applicants must have attended high school in an Alberta community at or north of that line, and sign a return of service agreement on completion.
metaDetail: Drawn on a map: high school north of the 54th.

title: Queen Elizabeth II Platinum Jubilee Citizenship Award
audience: Graduating Alberta Grade 12 students who hold a Premier's Citizenship Award nomination
notes: Your school nominates one graduating student for the Premier's Citizenship Award, and that nomination is what makes you eligible here, so the deadline that actually matters is your school's internal one. The 2027 intake opens March 1, 2027 and closes June 1, 2027 through the GATE Front Office system. The Alberta Centennial Award runs off the same nomination.
description: Eight young Albertans a year receive a $7,000 scholarship and a medallion for citizenship, leadership and community service, not for grades. You have to hold your school's Premier's Citizenship Award nomination first, be a Canadian citizen, permanent resident or protected person, be an Alberta resident, and be enrolled full time in a post-secondary program for the fall or winter term. The application wants a Record of Accomplishments chart covering your community work and two reference letters of no more than two pages each.

title: Optimist International Essay Contest
audience: Students under 19 who have not yet finished secondary school
notes: April 15 is the date your District has to send its winner to Optimist International, and the Districts send to that date every year. Your own deadline is set by your sponsoring club and is much earlier: club contests run in early February, and clubs pass their winner up by the end of that month. Contact a local club in the fall rather than waiting for a posted date. Alberta clubs sit in Zones 3, 5 and 6 of the AMSNW District.
description: Optimist International runs an annual essay contest with a set topic, and club winners advance to a District competition worth a $2,500 scholarship. You have to be under 19 as of October 1 of the contest year and not yet finished secondary school. Entries go through a local Optimist Club, and you have to enter in the District where you live, which for Alberta students is the Alberta, Montana, Saskatchewan and Northern Wyoming District.

title: Optimist International Oratorical Contest
audience: Students under 19 who have not yet finished secondary school
notes: No date is shown here because there is no single one to show. Club contests are usually held by late March but each sponsoring club sets its own, the Alberta Zone contest runs in April, and the District contest sits inside the third quarter District meeting in May. The date you need is your local club's, so contact one in the fall. Alberta clubs sit in Zones 3, 5 and 6 of the AMSNW District.
description: Optimist International runs an annual speech contest on a set topic, judged live rather than on paper. You have to be under 19 as of October 1 of the contest year and not yet finished secondary school. You start at a local Optimist Club and win your way up through the Zone to the District, where the placings are worth $2,500, $1,500 and $1,000. This is a sibling of the Communication Contest for the Deaf and Hard of Hearing, which runs the same topic on a separate track.
